name: Amaziah
bio:
Amaziah succeeded his father Joash as king of Judah after Joash was assassinated by two of his own servants and buried with his ancestors in the City of David (2 Kings 12:20-21).

## 📖 Core Story: Victory Over Edom, Defeat by Israel

Amaziah reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem, doing right in the LORD's eyes but not like David, following his father Joash's example; the high places remained. Once his throne was secure, he executed the servants who had killed his father, but spared their children, following the law of Moses that forbade punishing children for their parents' sins. He struck down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt and captured Sela, renaming it Joktheel (2 Kings 14:1-7).

Chronicles fills in how that victory came about. Amaziah first hired 100,000 Israelite mercenaries for a hundred talents of silver, but a man of God warned him that the LORD was not with Ephraim and he would be brought down if he took them into battle; though it cost him the silver already paid, Amaziah sent the Israelite troops home, infuriating them. He then led Judah's own army to the Valley of Salt, striking down ten thousand Edomites and throwing another ten thousand captives to their deaths off a cliff — while the dismissed Israelite mercenaries, in retaliation, raided Judah's towns on their way home, killing 3,000 and seizing plunder. Flush with victory, Amaziah then set up the gods of Edom as his own and worshiped them; when a prophet challenged him for bowing to gods that could not even save their own people from him, Amaziah cut him off and threatened him, and the prophet warned that God had determined to destroy him for his idolatry and for refusing to listen (2 Chronicles 25:1-16).

Flush with that victory, Amaziah challenged Jehoash, king of Israel, to battle. Jehoash warned him off with a parable about a thistle provoking a cedar, but Amaziah wouldn't listen — Chronicles notes this was God's doing, to hand Judah over for seeking the gods of Edom — and the two met at Beth Shemesh, where Judah was routed (2 Chronicles 25:17-20). Jehoash captured Amaziah, broke down part of Jerusalem's wall, and plundered the temple and palace treasuries before returning to Samaria (2 Kings 14:8-14). Amaziah lived fifteen more years after Jehoash's death, but was eventually assassinated by conspirators in Jerusalem; he fled to Lachish, where they caught and killed him anyway. He was buried in the City of David, and the people made his son Azariah king in his place (2 Kings 14:17-21).
